correctness.rationale: For identical additive two-agent valuations w_t∈{1,2}, maximum instantaneous pairwise envy equals absolute signed load gap. Folding any signed allocation gap mod 4 to distance in {0,1,2} never increases cost and realizes all folded transitions by valid allocations. The only optional edge is (state 1, unit good) ->0 or 2; selecting 0 instead of 2 cannot raise cumulative cost through the next unit, since intervening doubles alternate 0 and 2 and both paths meet at state 1 on the next unit. This proves greedy lower-load-first exactly optimal for each fixed order. The free-order lower bound from w_t<=|D_t|+|D_{t-1}|, parity, and the zero-return unit/double/mixed blocks gives u[b+ceil(a/2)+1_{a=0 and b odd}]. The u,u,3u,u counterexample genuinely beats greedy: 4u versus 6u. Independently tested all 4095 fixed words over {1,2} of lengths ≤11 against exact DP and all 81 count pairs a,b≤8 against free-order DP; proof, not testing, supplies unbounded quantifiers.
